item.title: Lancaster Breakfast and History Walking Tour — Fri Nov 20, 9:00 AM — Unique Lancaster
item.description:
Searching for a walking history tour in Lancaster? You’re in for a flavorful experience—literally!
Introducing the Lancaster History & Breakfast Walking Tour—a dynamic two-hour adventure that blends the rich heritage of one of America’s oldest inland cities with a delicious morning meal. Explore Lancaster’s vibrant streets with a professionally trained local guide and journey through time from the early 1700s through the transformative decades of the 20th century.
Brought to you by Unique Lancaster Experiences, this guided walk kicks off with your choice of hot or iced coffee or tea to energize your morning. Along the way, you’ll hear engaging stories about Lancaster’s evolution as a bustling Market City and its transition from trolleys to automobiles after WWI.
But this isn’t your standard history tour. You’ll dive into interactive discussions and uncover captivating insights about colonial life, architectural landmarks, and the impact of prohibition on the region.

item.title: ExtraGive: What Do You Love About Lancaster’s History? — Fri Nov 20, 5:00 PM — The Thaddeus Stevens & Lydia Hamilton Smith Center for History and Democracy
item.description:
What do you love about Lancaster’s history? The people? The places? The stories that shaped our community? This ExtraGive, LancasterHistory is celebrating it all, and they want you to be part of the fun!
Thaddeus Stevens & Lydia Hamilton Smith Center for History & Democracy! Drop in downtown between 5–8 PM for a special evening of Pay-What-You-Can admission at the Stevens & Smith Center! Explore their newest museum, discover a pop-up display featuring fascinating pieces of Lancaster’s history (some familiar favorites and others that might surprise you), and enjoy a special flash talk at 5:30 PM with Stephanie Townrow, LancasterHistory’s Director of Interpretation & Exhibitions.
Throughout the evening, hear from familiar community voices in a rotating video sharing what they love most about Lancaster’s history, and add your own through a fun, interactive display. item.title: Evening Compline — Mon Nov 23, 9:00 PM — Saint James Episcopal Church
item.description:
Evening Compline via Zoom Click here to join Compline. (This link can be used for every evening Compline on Zoom.)
The short service of Compline is based on the closing time of prayer in the Daily Office, or monastic cycle of prayer. It is observed in monasteries around 8 or 9 PM when darkness has fallen and bedtime is near.
The thoughts that inspire the prayers during Compline are the need for divine forgiveness and protection against the powers of darkness. Prayers for peace and rest are offered as night falls.
People of all faiths and beliefs are invited to this contemplative service. The service lasts about 20 minutes.
Source: Saint James Lancaster

Being One Center in Lancaster County Life can be frustrating and distressing! Sometimes we just feel overwhelmed, insecure, or lost!
The good news is, you're not alone!
We warmly invite you to check-in and connect with community in our Online Spiritual Support Group. In each meeting, we will discuss our current stressors and see how we can positively cope using our spiritual tools to overcome these challenges.

item.title: Swoon Squad: A Romance TBR Book Club — Mon Jan 25, 6:00 PM — Manheim Township
item.description:
Book Club, Adults, Seniors
Swoon Squad is a romance-centered book club with a twist. Instead of everyone reading the same assigned title, we choose a monthly trope and invite you to pick any book that fits the theme! Whether you're into sweet contemporary rom-coms, high-heat historical reads, or paranormal romance, there's a seat for you at our table! How it Works: Pick Your Own Adventure: We announce the month's trope, and you choose a book from your own TBR pile or the library shelves that features it. Low Pressure, High Fun: No more scrambling to finish a specific book you might not even like. Read at your own pace and bring your honest thoughts! The Discussion: We gather to swap recommendations, vent about our favorite (and least favorite) clichés, and discover new authors through each other's picks.Come ready to share your pick, discuss the tropes, and meet fellow romance fans in a comfortable library setting ❤️January 25: 🕰️Historical Romance🕰️February 22: 💍Fake Dating / Marriag

item.title: LFS Monthly Discussion - El Serrano's — Wed Feb 3, 6:00 PM
item.description:
Lancaster Freethought Society Come joins us for intelligent discussion and freethinking fun at our monthly meeting. Lancaster Freethought Society is a community for Freethinkers, Atheists, Agnostics, Humanists, Non-believers, Skeptics, and those who are simply curious. There is no fee to attend our meetings which range from topical subjects of interest to freethinkers such as Church/State Separation, as well as subjects such as science, philosophy, ethics, counter-apologetics, and psychology. All are welcome to attend no matter what your beliefs may be but proselytizing is not allowed. Bring your articles, news, jokes, gripes, questions, ideas, topics, or anything else you would like to discuss with the rest of the group.
Hope to see you there!
Source: Meetup: Lancaster Freethought Society

item.title: Dillsburg Game Night - Calvary Methodist Church in the Family Center — Wed Nov 25, 6:30 PM
item.description:
Central PA Game Club Dillsburg Game Night meets every Wednesday from 6:30-9:30pm for casual tabletop games. We’ve been going strong since 2016, and most Wednesdays you’ll find about 30-40 gamers who love to learn and teach new games. It’s a great group of friendly people.
Given the timeframe, most of the games played are light to medium Euros, although many of us also love card games (including trick-taking games) and party games. We have a library of about 200 games available to play, and people typically bring their own games as well.
We also run long game days (typically every other month, usually a Saturday 2-9pm) and other special events. Join us on Facebook or Discord for more information about those.
Attendees do not often RSVP on Meetup. It may show 1 person is coming but we have 40 people every Wednesday and will cancel the event if it is not happening. Feel free to message with questions.
Cost: Free Who: All Ages (15 and under must be accompanied by an adult) When: Every

item.title: Handling the Holidays: Keep Your Glow On ✨ — Tue Dec 8, 6:00 PM — Manheim Township
item.description:
Health & Wellness, Adults, Seniors
The holidays bring joy, but they can also bring overwhelm, busy schedules, and unexpected curveballs. Join us for an empowering session focused on staying grounded, protecting your peace, and navigating the season with confidence. We’ll cover practical boundary-setting, stress reduction, and thoughtful budget-friendly standby gift ideas ($25 and under!) so you’re prepared for whatever comes your way. item.title: Creating My Wellness Plan — Wed Dec 16, 5:30 PM — Lancaster
item.description:
Discussion, Teens
Teens are invited on a journey to create a personalized Wellness Recovery Action Plan (WRAP). WRAP is an evidence-based, interactive, psycho-educational course where teens will explore stressors, early warning signs, crisis planning and developing their own wellness toolbox. This six-week program will be led by Licensed Clinical Social Worker, Janae Allgire and Master's Level Social Worker, Ashlee Rineer. Session One: Intro to WrapSession Two: Wellness ToolboxSession Three: My Daily PlanSession Four: StressorsSession Five: Early Warning Signs & When Things Break DownSession Six: Crisis & Post-CrisisParticipants who attend at least four out of the six sessions will receive a Visa gift card worth $45. Space is limited · Registration is requiredAges 14-18This series is made possible by the LGBTQ+ Giving Circle & All Seasons Wellness LLC.

item.description:
Community, Adults, Seniors
Energy Efficiency and Electrification BasicsDoes your home feel cold this winter? Is your heating bill higher than it should be? Are you looking for ways to live in ways that are gentler on Planet Earth? Join Andrew Pauls-Thomas, Director of Energy Solutions at RegenAll for an overview of energy efficiency basics as well as ideas for reducing or eliminating fossil fuel use in your home. Andrew will touch on solutions to match every budget and every home – from simple DIY caulking to full replacement of your heating system.This program is in partnership with RegenAll, an organization that is committed to resilience and climate work done with communities, not for them. item.title: Evening Compline — Sat Nov 21, 9:00 PM — Saint James Episcopal Church
item.description:
Evening Compline via Zoom Click here to join Compline. (This link can be used for every evening Compline on Zoom.)
The short service of Compline is based on the closing time of prayer in the Daily Office, or monastic cycle of prayer. It is observed in monasteries around 8 or 9 PM when darkness has fallen and bedtime is near.
The thoughts that inspire the prayers during Compline are the need for divine forgiveness and protection against the powers of darkness. Prayers for peace and rest are offered as night falls.
People of all faiths and beliefs are invited to this contemplative service. The service lasts about 20 minutes.
Source: Saint James Lancaster

item.title: Children's Chapel — Sun Nov 22, 10:30 AM — Saint James Episcopal Church
item.description:
Children’s Chapel* meets weekly during the 10:30 AM Sunday Mass. Children and youth ages 3 and above begin the morning in the sanctuary where they can experience the processional and the opening congregational prayers. After the opening Collect, children are invited to the front of the sanctuary to make their way to the chapel and participate in songs, prayers, brief meditation and storytelling of the day’s Gospel and/or New and Old Testament readings. The Godly Play® teaching method includes using beautiful wooden figures, candles, and symbolic colors to aid our storytelling as we listen to God’s word for us. Children often respond to the story using simple art supplies including crayons, construction paper, origami paper and Model Magic air dry clay. Children return to the Sanctuary during the passing of the Peace. They are welcome to take part in Holy Communion.
Source: Saint James Lancaster

item.title: Vespers at the Urban Well — Sun Nov 22, 5:00 PM — Saint James Episcopal Church
item.description:
Vespers, Sunday evenings at 5:00 PM | In person only A contemplative candlelit service to nurture mind, body and spirit Join us Sunday evenings for Vespers, a warm and inviting weekly gathering in the serene surroundings of the Saint James Chapel. This quiet, reflective service embraces Christianity’s rich prayer traditions and the embodied practices that nurture our spiritual lives today. Gather with us for uplifting singing, find solace in moments of silence, and choose the posture that feels most comfortable as we open our hearts to listen for God’s voice and center ourselves for the week ahead. We have meditation cushions and chairs available for your comfort. We’ll celebrate Holy Communion on the third Sunday of the month. In person only. Everyone is welcome—come as you are!
Source: Saint James Lancaster
